entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.9.10r2
entry.content:
The skill book stops breaking after a save and quit.
Every relog used to leave the book drawing pieces of the game world — character models, monsters, the title flames — where its icons and frame should be, until the game was closed and started again. It has come and gone since the 2.x days, each fix moving it from one picture to another.
Measured this time: the pictures the mod loads from its own files were intact after the relog, at the same addresses, and still drew wrong. The renderer keeps a cache of decoded frames keyed on the picture's address and rebuilds that cache's memory when a game ends; a picture kept across the relog was a stale key pointing at recycled memory. So every one of them is now loaded afresh for each session, and the previous copy is released with the allocator that made it.
Two checks guard it: one that no picture loaded from disk is ever handed to the wrong free, and one that every such picture is reloaded per session.
Plugin and world file are unchanged from v3.9.10.

entry.title: Haste v0.5.1
entry.content:
The first revision to the fifth major release of the Haste Archipelago
You will need to subscribe to and enable the [Mod](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3462307025) on Steam.
## Logic Changes - The Triangular Distribution for Fragmentsanity can **no longer** be enabled with Dynamic Per-Shard Fragmentsanity, due to an emerging concern over seeds taking dozens of hours to finish a single late-game Shard's worth of fragment clears if the scaling was high enough - Triangular Distribution can still be used with Static Per-Shard and Global Fragmentsanities, and Balanced Triangular is unaffected - This restriction may be revisited at a later time, due to Triangular being a "landmine" setting that can catastrophically blow up expected seed times with certain combinations of settings - As an example: - With the maximum Dynamic Scaling of 200%, there would be **66** checks in Disaster Shard 2 (and onward), and would require **2211 Fragment clears** to attain - At a *generously* estimated 40 seconds per Fragment, it would roughly **24.5 hours** to complete *just* D2's Fragmentsanity checks - With the same scaling, Shard 1's 26 checks would take **3.9 hours** to complete - In total, from Shard 1 to D2, it would take at best **~120 hours** to do all 482 checks - **This is an unreasonable ask in basically any scenario** - However, at 100% scaling, it would take **30 hours** to complete its 241 checks. This is still a large value, but could hypothetically be playable in long asyncs
## Bugfixes - Fixed Shopsanity Scaling accidentally using Fragmentsanity Scaling's value in the slot data

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.9.12
entry.content:
Shop Shuffle now stocks the whole game. Every vendor draws its shelf from the complete item list on all three tabs — weapons, armor, gems, runes, jewels, charms, rings and amulets — and rolls them as normal, magic, rare, set and unique items. The game prices them itself, so the best pieces cost a fortune, and the shelf re-rolls whenever the vendor restocks. Potions, scrolls, keys and ammo stay exactly as before. Items you buy count for the Collection book.
The mod fills the shelf itself now. The engine walked the item table in file order, stopped after thirty rows and never rolled anything above magic, which is why every shop showed the same first handful of weapons. The vendor columns still come from the seed's tables, so an install without the mod's filler shows a plain slice of the same pool.
The launcher reads ItemTypes.txt out of your own archives, with a built-in copy as fallback. Without that table the shop deal did nothing on a fresh install.

entry.title: PAYDAY 2: Criminal Dawn v1.0.4r3
entry.content:
A continuous problem has been that the timing on White House is somewhat unfair and very tight, however in all my testing I tend to get Crude Awakening as the final heist instead so I was never really able to experience how rough it could be for myself. After replaying White House a couple times now (not in Criminal Dawn, just generally) I've realised that, yeah. White House *is* a lot longer than I previously thought it was - a well executed loud playthrough can take 20 minutes minimum.
Because I kept getting Crude Awakening in testing, a lot of the timer balance was tailored around *that* heist instead - the issue with this is Crude Awakening can be easily completed in about *ten* minutes, half the time of White House. This creates a huge time gap, and makes White House incredibly unfair to get as the final heist, which is why a lot of people have (rightfully!!) complained about it.
All this is to say White House now benefits from Objectivity when it's chosen as the final heist, *but* you only receive 50% of the bonus instead of the entire bonus. If you have 60% objective speed, you will get 30% on White House. 90% objective speed, you get 45% on White House - etc.
_No APWorld changes since v1.0.4._

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.9.13
entry.content:
Fixes from Testing Round 1.
**XP multiplier came back at 0x after every relaunch** (BetaHub #22). The multiplier is read from the seed when a character is created, and the state file's copy is deliberately not trusted under Archipelago, so an existing character loaded with standard XP no matter what the YAML said. The player-side settings (XP multiplier, skill cap, skill level requirements) now follow the seed on every character load.
**Hellfire Torch arrived as a Magic Large Charm** (BetaHub #26). Hellfire Torch and Annihilus have item level 110 in the game's own table, and the delivery never tried above 99, so the unique roll could not pass and the engine handed back a magic charm. Uniques are now created at their own level.
**Shrines, urns, barrels and chests now fire their check every time.** The escalating chance (10% to 100%) is a YAML option, "Bonus Checks Random Chance", off by default. Seeds generated before this release stop rolling and become guaranteed; the number of locations is unchanged either way.
**The unstuck message names the skill.** "Fists of Fire cannot be used with this weapon" instead of "that skill" (BetaHub #21 and #23). The three elemental Martial Arts charge-ups are claw-only in the base game; the engine freezes the character rather than refusing, and the watchdog frees them.
Plugin 1.2.16 carries the new YAML option in Create YAML.

Both are now multiplied by a new YAML option, "Gold Cap Multiplier", default 30: a level-10 character carries 3M, and the stash holds 33M from the start. Both limits stop at 33,000,000 because the save file stores gold in 25 bits.

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.9.16
entry.content:
**Items no longer vanish from the cursor.** Every item the launcher delivers goes in through the game's own quest-item routine, which puts the new item wherever there is room. When the player was holding an item mid-drag, that room was the cursor, and the held item was gone (BetaHub #25: a weapon lost the moment a Flawless Gem arrived).
Item rewards and boss loot now wait while anything is on the cursor. The queue keeps them; they arrive the tick after the item is put down. A hold longer than a click shows "Items wait until you put that down" so a delayed delivery reads as waiting, not lost.
Gold, XP, stat and skill points are unaffected and still arrive at once.

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.9.20
entry.content:
**Skill points no longer move between skills on relog.** At exit the mod reads each button's level out of the save file to reinvest it after the reset. The game writes those bytes in class-skill-list order, and the mod fills that list compactly, empty buttons skipped, so a button's level sits at "number of filled buttons before it", not at the button's own index. The mod read the wrong byte for every button after the first gap: one skill picked up another's level, the real owner read 0 and fell back to the click cache, and the pool clamp then zeroed the last row. Nothing was lost — the total was constant across cycles — but points wandered on every relog. The read now follows the same compact order the list is written in. Verified against a live log where save bytes 9 to 12 held exactly the levels of buttons 13, 20, 21 and 22.
Points that ended up unspent are in your pool; spend them again once and they stay put.
Plugin stays at 1.2.19.

entry.title: Minishoot Adventures v0.6.0
entry.content:
## [0.6.0] - 2026-09-05
### Added
- A new setting called "Split Surf" has been added. - When enabled, each water type requires its own Surf item to be navigable. - When disabled, the normal Surf item unlocks navigation on all water types. - Will replace Surf and 4 filler items. - Water types are: Normal, Blue, Soiled, Dungeon and Gold. - Logic has been adjusted to accomodate this new setting. - Each surf items will be visible in the inventory. - A new setting called "Split Supershot" has been added. - When enabled, the Supershot is broken down into 2 distinct items. - Blastshot allows you to break rocks and walls. - Flameshot allows you to light torches. - Having one these two items will unlock Supershot for combat usage. - When enabled, Supershot and one filler item will be replaced. - Logic has been adjusted to accomodate this new setting. - Both of these items will be visible in the inventory. - A new setting called "Primordial Crystal Activation Threshold" has been added. - Set the Primordial Crystal activation threshold. - If your current HP percentage is greater than or equal to this value and you have the Primordial Crystal, it will activate. - This allows for more flexibility in the use of the Primordial Crystal, especially in combination with the "Enable Primordial Crystal Logic" option. - This option does not affect logic. The value must be between 10 and 100. - A new setting called "Progressive Boost" has been added. - When enabled, the game will fuse the Boost and the Advanced Energy module into two cumulative progressive upgrades. - The first upgrade will always allow you to boost, and the second will reduce the energy cost of boosting. - Note that both instances of Progressive Boost are marked as "Progression", although the second upgrade does not unlock any location. - A new setting called "Progressive Powers" has been added. - When enabled, the game will fuse all powers and the corresponding idols into two cumulative progressive upgrades. - The first upgrade will always allow you to use the corresponding power, and the second will grant you the idol's effect. - Note that both instances of Progressive Power of protection are marked as "Progression", although the second upgrade does not unlock any location. - The APWorld now has a manifest.
### Changed
- **IMPORTANT** Some settings and location names have been renamed. See [docs/dev/history/0-6-0-renames.md](docs/dev/history/0-6-0-renames.md) for the full list. - This means that you must change your YAML settings file for Archipelago. Refer to the file above for the replacements. - Fixed "Dungeon 3 - Behind North West doors" logic : now properly check for a way to use springboards - Necessary to unlock the door to said location. - All shop locations requiring Super Crystals are now locked behind the same conditions as clearing Dungeon 5. - As of now, there is no guarantee to have a sufficient amount of Super Crystals to buy the items you need. - This is temporary, as work on this very subject will begin soon-ish. - When the goal is set to "Spirit Tower", the Golden Crystal Heart will now replace a filler item, instead of an Ancient Tablet.
### Known issues
- Rarely, when hovering between a piece of land and a piece of water, Minishoot can fall.

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.9.21
entry.content:
**Zone locks no longer follow you from one difficulty into another.** The mod keeps one lock table and built it once, at character load, from the difficulty stored in the state file. That is the difficulty of the previous session, not of the game being joined. A player who last saved in Hell and then made a Normal game got Hell's locks, nothing received there yet so everything shut, laid over Normal, and a final region they had already cleared was locked again. Keys received in the new game then poked holes in a table that belonged to a different difficulty.
Character load now reads the difficulty from the live game before building the table and before the load-time reconcile, and every difficulty change during play rebuilds the table from that difficulty's own keys. Quest completions, area kills, gate-boss kills, waypoints, level milestones and gate-key receipts were already tracked per difficulty; the lock table was the only piece that was not, so nothing else moves.
Verified against a live log: character loaded with the stored difficulty 2 (Hell), locks applied for Hell, first tick reported "Difficulty change: 2 -> 0" with no rebuild. That is the sequence this fixes.
Plugin stays at 1.2.19.
